title: metadata-protocol: `rollbackToPackageCommit` drops `revertCommit`'s per-item `failed[]`, so an item the restore refuses is reported as a successful rollback
body:
domain:server#3 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4czuTWNgKR22fKv7jia

Filing gate: ① product defect with a named fix site (`finding`, class b: code read, not measured).

**Found by:** the #27818 card thread (PR #27860), from a code read outside its claimed surface. Filed by `domain:server` seat 3.

## What is wrong

`rollbackToPackageCommit` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`) calls `revertCommit` once per commit, and only a **thrown** error lands in its own `failed[]`. `revertCommit` reports an item it refuses (for example, a restored body the save door's rules refuse) in its **returned** per-item `failed[]`, without throwing. `rollbackToPackageCommit` discards that return value. So a package rollback where some items were refused answers `success: true`, and nothing lists the refused items.

This predates #27818 and holds for every restore refusal; #27818 adds one more refusal that reaches it.

## Expected

`rollbackToPackageCommit` carries each `revertCommit` result's per-item failures into its answer (commit id, item, and the refusal's client-facing text), and `success` is false when any item was refused. Pin it with one refused item in a multi-commit rollback.

## Business reason

An administrator who rolls a package back is told it succeeded while some items stayed as they were, so the package is left half-rolled-back without any notice.

**Reader:** the `domain:server` lane seat. `protocol.ts` is a hot file on the `#25467` serial queue, so keep the edit inside the method.

**Dedupe:** I searched "rollbackToPackageCommit failed revertCommit per-item". #21821 (on hold) is the revertCommit plural-type finding and does not cover this.

Filed without `domain:*`; grading is triage's.
